opening_message:
Ticket 1: Keith Mclaughlin (employee ID E032) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E032.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Employee E032 (Keith Mclaughlin) is a full-time Analyst. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write; Analyst does not own Source Code, so admin is not applicable. Write is within policy — recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E032 (Keith Mclaughlin) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as previously noted. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Basic training caps access at read; requested write exceeds this, so recommend granting read.
reason: Security note indicates E032 is a contractor with basic security training (correcting the HR note's full-time classification). Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Since training is basic, the maximum allowed level is read. The requested write exceeds the maximum, so grant the maximum: read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee is Keith Mclaughlin (E032), requesting write access to Source Code.

There are two notes - HR says full-time Analyst, Security says contractor with basic security training. These conflict.

Key facts:
- Access levels: none, read, write, admin
- Policy: full_time employees up to write; admin only if role owns system. Contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

HR note: full-time Analyst, recommends write.
Security note: contractor, basic security training, recommends read.

The Security agent's note references the HR note ("not full-time as previously noted") - suggesting the HR note written first was corrected by Security. Security DB shows contractor with basic training.

Since there's a conflict, I need to decide. The Security note seems to be a correction - it says "not full-time as previously noted." Security is likely more authoritative on employment type/training. 

So the employee is a contractor with basic security training. Max access: read (contractor with basic training = read; write requires advanced training).

Requested: write. Above maximum (read), so grant maximum: read.

I'll submit decision: read.
